complexity_scope.guarantee: Deterministic guaranteed success for a valid promise; finite schedule and sound acceptance for either radius validity.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: O_p constants depend only on p; log_+ uses natural logarithm. No arithmetic/bit-complexity or uniform-in-p bound.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact feasible G-jets through p-1; for known G=F+a id+b, one G-query uses one original-F query plus known affine data.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Evaluated feasible normal certificate of norm <=delta, or Failure under an invalid distance promise.
complexity_scope.regime: Fixed integer p>=2; positive Lp,mu,R,delta; original compact convex domain retained.
complexity_scope.resource: <=2 sum_{j<J}T_p(R/2^j,mu)+2 original queries, including all nested calls and final evaluation.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper witness: Algorithm 2 BaseTrial with Algorithm 1 stages and a final full model correction.

content.intended_use: Certify BaseTrial success for a valid radius and finite, sound behavior for a false radius.

dependencies.role: Distance-halving guarantee under each valid stage promise

dependencies: Source Lemmas 4.1–4.2 for Taylor remainder and exact-model normal
proofs.full_local_argument: Use the exact model and genuine normal from source Lemmas 4.1–4.2. Let s=y-x, E=G(y)-Gbar_x(y), and v=G(y)+n=E-beta||s||^(p-1)s. Taylor's bound is ||E||<=Lp||s||^p/p!. Since 0 in G(z_star)+N_X(z_star), monotonicity of G+N_X implies <v,y-z_star>>=0. If s is nonzero, ||x-z_star||<=r gives <s,y-z_star>>=||s||^2-||s||r and ||y-z_star||<=||s||+r. Consequently beta||s||^(p-1)(||s||^2-||s||r)<=||E||(||s||+r), hence beta(||s||-r)<=Lp(||s||+r)/p!. Substituting beta=2p Lp/p! yields (2p-1)||s||<=(2p+1)r and thus ||s||<=3r. If s=0, this bound is immediate. For either case, ||v||<=||E||+beta||s||^p<=(2p+1)Lp||s||^p/p!<=A_p Lp r^p. One jet at x constructs the model and one query at y evaluates the certificate, for at most two queries. Now initialize z=w, r=R. Under the valid promise, Proposition 4.5 inductively guarantees ||z-z_star||<=r after each z=Halve(G,z,mu,r), r=r/2 update. At loop termination A_p Lp r^p<=delta; the correction estimate ensures that the evaluated final norm test passes. For any supplied R>0, regardless of promise validity, after exactly J=max{0,ceil(log_2(A_p Lp R^p/delta)/p)} scheduled halvings its radius threshold is met. Each Halve has at most 2T_p calls and the correction at most two, giving the displayed finite bound. Set q=2/(p+1) and K=[2b_p(4/3)^((p-1)/2)]^q. Since max{1,ceil(t)}<=1+t for t>=0, T_p(R/2^j,mu)<=1+K(Lp R^(p-1)/mu)^q 2^(-2j(p-1)/(p+1)). Therefore the sum is at most J plus K(Lp R^(p-1)/mu)^q/[1-2^(-2(p-1)/(p+1))]. Also J<=1+log_+(A_p Lp R^p/delta)/(p log 2). This proves the O_p expression, including the final additive correction cost. Without a valid radius, the distance induction and small-residual estimate can fail; the schedule does not change. The exact model still supplies n in the original N_X(y), G(y) is actually queried, and the algorithm returns success only after checking ||G(y)+n||<=delta. Thus no accepted false certificate is possible. Known affine regularization changes the value and Jacobian by known terms only, so every counted G-query is simulated with one original-F query; the highest-derivative Lipschitz bound is unchanged for p>=2.

assumptions: G is C^(p-1) on an open neighborhood of X and Lip(D^(p-1)G)<=Lp on X in multilinear operator norm.
G is mu-strongly monotone on X; mu>0 is supplied.
w in X; exact feasible jets through D^(p-1)G and exact known-domain model/projection operations.
For guaranteed success, ||w-z_star||<=R. The finite schedule and sound acceptance do not require this distance promise.
statement.conclusion: With ||w-z_star||<=R, BaseTrial returns (y,n,G(y)) with y in X, n in N_X(y), evaluated G(y), and ||G(y)+n||<=delta. For J=max{0,ceil(log_2(A_p Lp R^p/delta)/p)}, its query count is <=2 sum_{j=0}^{J-1}T_p(R/2^j,mu)+2=O_p(1+(Lp R^(p-1)/mu)^(2/(p+1))+log_+(A_p Lp R^p/delta)). This scheduled bound also holds for a false radius; the genuine final normal and explicit norm test prevent acceptance of a false certificate, although Failure is possible. Reusable correction: if ||x-z_star||<=r, the model gives ||y-x||<=3r and ||G(y)+n||<=A_p Lp r^p using <=2 original queries including evaluation. These are the unnumbered equation (4.12)/Algorithm 2 guarantees, not a Proposition 4.6.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Known nonempty compact convex original X subset R^d, diam(X)<=D; Euclidean vector norm and induced multilinear norm. N_X(y)={n:<n,u-y><=0 for every u in X}. z_star is the unique solution of the G-VI. Define b_p=2p/p!, beta=b_p Lp=2Lp/(p-1)!, A_p=(2p+1)3^p/p!, log_+(s)=max{0,log s}. At center x the full model is Gbar_x(y)=sum_{j=0}^{p-1}D^jG(x)[y-x]^j/j! and 0 in Gbar_x(y)+beta||y-x||^(p-1)(y-x)+N_X(y), with n=-Gbar_x(y)-beta||y-x||^(p-1)(y-x).
statement.parameter_domains: d>=1; fixed integer p>=2; D,Lp,mu,R,delta>0. No smaller localization domain is introduced. Taking R<=D is available for the later adaptive wrapper, but is not needed for Algorithm 2's stated finite schedule.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such admissible G and all positive supplied parameters, deterministic Algorithm 2 has a finite schedule. For every valid radius promise it succeeds; for an invalid radius it can succeed or fail, but any returned certificate is genuine.

summary: A valid supplied radius guarantees an evaluated normal certificate with the p-dependent equation (4.12) query cost. The same finite scheduled cost holds for a false radius, and accepted certificates remain sound.
